- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.  
- If true price deviates from recent 7-day mean by >2%, model often fails to revert; apply mean reversion bias toward 7-day average for next 10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply downward adjustment of 1–4% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated reversal (e.g., 1.00 → -1.00 → 0.00), model often misses turning points; adjust forecast to align with sentiment shift direction 2–3 days ahead.
